summary: Clean on the SEC dimension. _c.py is a set of thin 1:1 libc pass-through wrappers; every pointer/length argument is forwarded unchanged to libc, which is the documented trusted-by-contract surface (the caller owns the buffer and the length exactly as when calling libc from C). The headline platform-variable-type hazard (long/time_t 32-bit on Win64) does not apply: none of the wrapped functions take long/time_t/clock/time/strtol/fseek/ftell, and the only platform-variable type present (size_t, modeled as intp) is 64-bit on every supported 64-bit CI platform, where intp is also 64-bit, so the register passing matches. The security-relevant lifetime/NUL hazards are all correctly documented in the wrapper docstrings (getenv environ ownership, strerror non-thread-safe static buffer, strncpy no-NUL-guarantee, fopen fclose ownership). No reachable corruption/crash/disclosure introduced by numbox.
